Plot component planes of a self-organising map

Source: R/plot_functions.R
eemsom_plot_cplane.Rd

A component plane shows the value of one variable in the prototypes of all units. Similar component planes indicate correlated variables. For maps of EEMs, the variables are wavelength pairs, for maps of PARAFAC loadings (eempf_som), the variables are the PARAFAC components.

Usage

eemsom_plot_cplane(som, ex = NULL, em = NULL, comps = NULL, scale = "common")

Arguments

som

object of class eemsom, see eemsom or eempf_som

ex

numeric vector of excitation wavelengths (maps of EEMs only)

em

numeric vector of emission wavelengths, same length as ex. Each pair of ex and em gives one component plane.

comps

numeric vector or names of PARAFAC components (maps of PARAFAC loadings only). NULL (default) plots all components.

scale

"common" (default) uses one colour scale for all component planes, so values can be compared between planes. "each" scales each component plane from 0 (minimum) to 1 (maximum), which shows patterns of weak peaks or components more clearly.

Value

a ggplot object

Details

The closest wavelengths available in the data are used. With scale = "common", values are on the scale of the normalised data.

Ejarque-Gonzalez and Butturini (2014) compared the component planes of all wavelength pairs by their correlation to discriminate fluorescence components, see eemsom_regions.

References

Ejarque-Gonzalez, E., Butturini, A. (2014). Self-Organising Maps and Correlation Analysis as a Tool to Explore Patterns in Excitation-Emission Matrix Data Sets and to Discriminate Dissolved Organic Matter Fluorescence Components. PLoS ONE 9(6), e99618. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0099618

See also

Other plots: eemsom_plot_map(), eemsom_plot_silhouette(), eemsom_plot_stability(), eemsom_plot_training(), ggeem.eemsom(), ggeem.eemsom_regions()

Examples

data(eem_list)

som <- eemsom(eem_list, rlen = 100, seed = 42)
# fluorescence peaks B, T, A and C (Coble 1996)
eemsom_plot_cplane(som, ex = c(275, 275, 260, 350), em = c(310, 340, 450, 450))

eemsom_plot_cplane(som, ex = c(275, 275, 260, 350), em = c(310, 340, 450, 450), scale = "each")


data(pf_models)
pfsom <- eempf_som(pf4[[1]], rlen = 100, seed = 42)
eemsom_plot_cplane(pfsom, scale = "each")
